title: The Soul as Mother and the Nature of Israel
english: He is both maker and provider of all things. These things he says, not separating the Son from the Father or the Father from the Son; for the divinity is one, and there is no other God besides the Son and no other the Father.

In Isaiah, indeed, concerning the Father, it is said: 'In you is God, and there is no God besides you; for you are God, and we are not afraid' (Isa 25:6-7). For if there were another God in the Son who is beside him, how could he subsequently bring forth: 'And there is no God besides you?' and immediately: 'For you are God, and we are not afraid, the God of Israel is Savior'? Therefore, even concerning the Father, when it is [said], 'Who is like our God, the Lord?' (Isa 40:25), the Son has not been excluded; but even concerning the Savior, the Father has not been set apart from the one divinity of Father and Son.

Who says: 'Who is the Lord our God, the one dwelling in the heights and looking down upon the lowly things?' For all lowly creatures and works are toward God, not only those upon the earth but also those in the heavens. And he sees these lowly things providentially.

For he sees the poor man cast down upon the earth and the needy man upon the refuse, and he raises them up from those standing in evils of want and poverty; and not merely to raise and make stand, but strengthening their goodness, seating them with rulers, preparing them to be equal to them. And he will seat them not with simple rulers, but with the rulers of his own people. And a woman, formerly dwelling in barrenness, will become a mother having borne many children.

It can also be said concerning the people from among the Gentiles, for whom the prophecy is: 'For this the poor people shall bless you' (Gal 3:14). Therefore, having raised this poor and needy people from the lowly things and from the refuse of Greek customs, he will seat them with the rulers of Israel, being their people. And the apostles are the rulers of the Hebrew people, whom we say are sitting on twelve thrones to judge the twelve tribes of Israel.

And the church from among the Gentiles, formerly barren, is called into joy, saying: 'Rejoice, barren one who does not bear children; break forth and cry out, you who do not labor in childbirth; for many more are the children of the desert than of her who has a man' (Isa 54:1). For truly, the church from among the Gentiles has become very much with children, more than she who has [a man].

The law of the man is the assembly of the Jews. Every soul, through chastity, is inhabited by God as a child in the church of the living God, a mother working out thoughts and words to rejoice in the offspring produced by the Word of God dwelling within her. This also happened according to the history of the Scripture. For instance, Anna, the mother of Samuel, is called a mother inhabiting the church, a mother having become such from children, rejoicing in children. And concerning Sarah and Rebekah and Elizabeth, and before this mother, the one born to Samson, someone says wisely concerning each of them what inhabited her: a mother of children, rejoicing (Ps 113:1,2).

For the intellect: the mind, seeing God, becomes like the wing of the things opposed to the truth, withdrawing from the dwellings of Egypt so as to no longer 'Egyptize,' nor to be contained by Egyptian superstitions, but to implore God, who sanctifies the soul that confesses sincerely; and he shall have authority and the king shall hold the discerning one. For Judah is confession, but Israel is the intellect seeing God. Previously, it was not fitting to confess, but now, since one has become a sanctuary of God, and His holy temple is being constructed, thus, having been perfected through the vision of the truth, Israel shall be shown to have come under the authority of God in order to be able to reign under Him, about to experience blessedness, seeing God with a pure heart (Ps 113:10,11).

'Where is their God?' the mortals say, when You, Lord, are doing us good. For they have local gods established in places, and they mock You by this, saying, 'Where is their God?' Perhaps they say this mockingly, thinking we have no God. But even if those wandering say this, we do not hold the precise opinion that our God is in the heavens above, but we think of Him not locally, but with a superabundance of majesty. For if He were in a place, He would be prevented from being elsewhere. And there is also a cause for all the heavens and upon the earth, since whatever He willed, He made, surpassing all things. Therefore, He is not contained by all things, but is also outside all things and exists in them according to the logic of creation and providence. For thus He fills the...

title: The Heavenly Heaven and the Trinity
english: heaven and the earth. But if all the heavens and those in them, the earth and all that is in it, should come into being as the essence of God's will, some are very impiously thinking and suddenly snatching away the substance of the Son, the will of the Father, making him a will of those in the heavens who are substantial. But let the impious hear how creation alone was subject to the will of God. For it is fitting for the Maker that he wills to create (God and James agree in writing: 'Having willed, he brought us forth,' [Rom 8:28] as he says in the word of God, a word of truth, so that we might be a kind of firstfruits of his own creatures and works) that the will of God be the cause. But the Son is neither a creature nor a work; he is a generation not of essence, but of will. For if he were a son of will, he would be an image and a character of God's will; but the divine words say he is the exact imprint of his hypostasis and an image of the invisible God. If the Son is not the exact imprint of the hypostasis and an image of the invisible God, then it is fitting that the Only-begotten be a generation of the essence of the invisible God and of his hypostasis. For indeed, those being born by the word of truth, they are such; and the Word and the Truth himself is the Only-begotten of God. Since he is not brought forth by a word of truth, he himself is the will of the Father; for in the same way that wisdom and truth are, so also the will of God is. Indeed, it is the same in wisdom and in will to do all things.

All the perceptive race has the mind to see God (Israel signifies by chance the church of the living God) [Ps 113:17] and hopes in the Lord, whereas all other men hope for nothing. And the one who is among those healing the divine, by chance being a priest, hopes in a greater Lord and in a hope witnessed by Israel; for of those who have ascended above by contemplation and practice, the hope is greater, asking more greatly to have him as a helper and a defender. But also all those fearing the Lord (these are not the proselytes and those added to the law from the Gentiles) hoping themselves in the Lord, call upon him to be a helper and a defender [Ps 113:20-21]. For God remembers all of those who have remembered him.

Remaining in memory. Therefore he says, 'Seek the law of your God, and I will seek [you],' children of yours. For the one forgetting the divine law immediately forgets also that which was given to him; but when a god remembers something blessed, he immediately turns toward it, giving spiritual and heavenly blessings according to the proportion of the greatness of faith, just as he gives the other gifts. Stand firm, for it is necessary for the small ones to receive [blessings] along with the great ones, among those alone fearing the Lord, and upon all the mentioned ranks, so that you may not differ in these things, where some are great and others small.

Blessed are we by the Lord, who made heaven and earth (Ps 113:23). For it is not that we observe the laws. Lest anyone think the divinations belong to another, Moses served; following this, the hierophant handed down the things concerning creation before the giving of the laws, through which he teaches that there is a God, but all the parts of the world and He himself are created. But he who wishes to contemplate these things more deeply will say that something is exceptionally said in the Scripture, a heaven characterized for God, in which God alone is; but I speak of God concerning the Trinity.

This heaven, far from being a place, is a property of essence for the created things, as these things are in the heavens. Take care lest, before the transgression, the devil, who finds himself below this heaven as in heaven, said, 'I will ascend into heaven, and above the stars of heaven I will set my throne' (Ps 113:24); for these things were said to him before he fell from heaven; indeed, this is also remembered as the cause of his fall. No one has ascended into this heaven except the one descending from heaven, since having been sent from there, he has come, saying, 'I have descended from heaven.' But also the Holy Spirit was sent from this heaven, which Peter says: 'Truly it has been announced to us through those who evangelized us by the Holy Spirit sent from heaven' (2 Pet 1:21). For the Father, and the Son, and the Holy Spirit [are thus]. But stand firm, lest you carry the thought concerning these things down to sensible things, supposing a local heaven and a movement occurring there by transport; for God's...

title: The Humility of John and the Eternal Truth
english: The preceding description of the heaven mentioned signifies a superiority and a state of being, if one may say so. None of those deadened by sin praises God (for a beautiful praise is not in the mouth of a sinner, Ps 113:25-26), nor do those descending into the tropical Hades become those who die the death following sin (for there is no one remembering God in death, Ps 114:6), nor anyone in Hades confessing himself.

Therefore, since they do not praise Him, we who live and partake of eternal life praise Him, concerning which the Savior says, 'And this is the eternal life, that they may know you, the only true God, and whom you sent, Jesus Christ' (John 17:3). The Lord himself protects those who, according to the commandment of Jesus, are childlike in turning and becoming, so that enemies do not attack them before the time of struggle. Just as He protects those who are such children, He humbled me, having set me against a struggle, as if I had ascended far above the age of children, and instead of being tested by many strong things, He made me; and just as He humbled me, so also He saved me, having clothed me with a strength surpassing the struggle and an invincible panoply.

Regarding this word, the Apostle says to the Corinthians, 'Having this, we have the same spirit of faith, according to what is written: I believed, therefore I spoke; and we also believe, therefore we also speak' (2 Cor 4:13). By saying 'spirit of faith,' he signifies the being which is near from it, the spirit provided by God to the one having faith. 'I believed, therefore I spoke' is in accord with the heart, for it is believed in the heart unto righteousness, but with the mouth it is confessed unto salvation; for he says, 'If you confess the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved' (Rom 10:9). For by this one is immediately brought to the heart, for it is believed in the heart unto righteousness, and the following. You will also receive this understanding, and 'If you do not believe, you will not understand' (Acts 5:25); for first one believes, if he understands, and after this he speaks, as the Psalm says, 'I believed, therefore I spoke.' When, having believed, I spoke exceedingly and great things, then, seeing nothing of myself, I was greatly humbled. Such is that which is [said] by John concerning Jesus.

Regarding the saying, 'That He must increase and I must decrease,' John was not diminishing in terms of actual magnitude, but was comparing himself to the superiority of Jesus's teaching and way of life (John 3:30). He who said, after speaking from the beginning, that he had believed, 'I have become exceedingly humbled,' did not suffer this by a subtraction of honor, but by seeing the greater and above himself. If even the death of many signifies God, those who die with Christ and carry His death in the flesh, and who recognized how well to give thanks, will receive the cup of such a saving death, and he who receives it will drink it blamelessly, if he calls upon the name of the Lord to drink it bravely.

If we have said of the lesser ones that they call upon the name of the Lord, let it not trouble you now to receive the Lord while not yet perfect; for the saints, being blind, give the lesser things to themselves that they possess. For Moses and Samuel did not say of themselves, 'We called upon the Lord,' but it is said of others. The word concerning salvation is not complete unless the memory of the saved is also taken up. For having said in that [psalm] as the end of the shadow approaching, 'I will offer to You a sacrifice of thanksgiving' (Ps 116:1), he immediately calls all nations into eternity, just as these also offer a sacrifice of thanksgiving through the ages, after one nation and people has been cast away, since a sinful nation and people having become full of sins is tossed about. But after this nation and people has been cast away, the mercy of God has reached all, as a certain and strong thing for His mercy to become upon us. And because this has surpassed, 'The truth of the Lord remains forever' (Ps 117:2). For the truth accepted the shadow as an end and a lot, limiting it, but the truth itself, being eternal, will receive nothing that is nothing above it, but itself above all, in an incomparable excess.
